title: Functorial mapping cocones and their specified signed shift comparisons
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with integer cochain complexes, mapping cones and shifts as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For chain maps $\varphi:K\to L$, $\psi:K^\prime\to L^\prime$ and a commuting square $(a,b)$ with $b\varphi=\psi a$, define the mapping-cocone map $\operatorname{Cone}(\varphi)[-1]\to\operatorname{Cone}(\psi)[-1]$ by shifting the diagonal mapping-cone map induced by $(a,b)$. For any category $S$, functors $F,G:S\to\operatorname{CochainComplex}(\mathcal A,\mathbb Z)$ and natural transformation $\tau:F\to G$, define the functor $C_\tau(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(\tau_X)[-1]$ on maps by this construction for $(F(f),G(f))$. For every chain map $\varphi$ and integer $m$, specify the signed comparison $\operatorname{Cone}(\varphi[m])[-1]\cong(\operatorname{Cone}(\varphi)[-1])[m]$ as $(-1)^m$ times the inverse standard cone-shift comparison shifted by $[-1]$, followed by the canonical interchange of shifts. If $S$ has integer shifts, $F,G$ have coherent shift comparisons and $\tau$ commutes with them, define $C_\tau(X[m])\cong C_\tau(X)[m]$ by the mapping-cocone isomorphism of the square of these comparisons, followed by that signed comparison. These specified component isomorphisms define the natural isomorphism $C_\tau\circ[m]\cong[m]\circ C_\tau$ (shift first on the left, shift last on the right). This definition specifies the data; the zero and successive-shift coherence laws are separate assertions.
